Title: The Busy Chat
Description: Your building chat has 300 members, but ten people write almost every message. Whose views do you collect first?
First option tooltip: You get replies quickly from across the building, but frequent posters may drown out quieter residents.
Second option tooltip: You hear from residents who rarely post. Visiting flats takes much longer.

Title: One Pick or Ranking
Description: Residents could pick one proposal or rank them all. Supporters of a playground and of extra benches worry that their proposals will split the vote. Which ballot will you build?
First option tooltip: The ballot is quick to build and easy to explain. Related proposals may split the vote.
Second option tooltip: Ranking can give related proposals a fairer chance. The team needs more time to explain it, especially to older voters.

Title: A Family Referral
Description: The OSI chair recommends his nephew, a developer who can start this week. He will work for half the usual pay. How will you hire?
First option tooltip: You save 200 and fill the post quickly. Some residents question whether the team can challenge the chair.
Second option tooltip: Residents can see why you picked the developer. The search takes longer and you lose the discount.

Title: Voting Without Smartphones
Description: Many older residents have no smartphone. They say an online ballot leaves them out. How will you include them?
First option tooltip: Residents can vote without a phone. Entering votes takes staff time and can introduce errors.
Second option tooltip: Helpers let residents use the existing ballot on shared devices. Training and transport cost 100.

Title: First on the Ballot
Description: A nearby property developer needs parking for its new building. It offers to sponsor the project if parking appears first on the ballot. Do you take the deal?
First option tooltip: You gain 300 for development. Residents may think the developer bought an advantage.
Second option tooltip: You can tell residents how you kept the ballot independent. You give up 300 in funding.

Title: Forty Overnight Ballots
Description: Just before the pilot vote closes, the OSI chair brings 40 overnight paper ballots for parking. Many are from eligible owners who rent out their flats, but no one has verified the signatures. What will you do?
First option tooltip: You follow the paper ballot rules and close the vote on time. Parents quit the pilot and say the app favours the loudest neighbour.
Second option tooltip: Each owner, including those who live elsewhere, uses an SMS or eGov code to prove their vote is genuine. Building the check costs 200 and delays the vote.

Title: A Running Tally
Description: Residents want to see the totals while the vote is still open. They say a running tally would bring more neighbours to the ballot. When will you show the results?
First option tooltip: A running tally draws more voters. Some late voters may follow the leader.
Second option tooltip: Voters choose without knowing which proposal is ahead. Fewer residents may return to cast a vote.

Title: The District Report
Description: The district office wants to explain the pilot in its report. It offers funding in exchange for the full list of who voted for what. What will you share?
First option tooltip: You gain 300 in district funding. Officials can see how each resident voted.
Second option tooltip: The district can report the result and voters keep their choices private. You give up the funding this time.

Title: Licensing for Reuse
Description: A company wants to sell a version of your tool to large housing managers. You have to choose the terms under which it can reuse your code. Which licence will you use?
First option tooltip: More companies may adopt the tool. They can sell versions with changes they keep closed.
Second option tooltip: Adapted versions that companies distribute must stay open. Some companies may choose another tool.

Title: A Late Compromise
Description: In a second pilot, residents propose splitting the courtyard between parking and a playground. The ballot is already open. When will you offer the compromise?
First option tooltip: Voters can choose a compromise that has local support. People who already voted must vote again.
Second option tooltip: You can finish the count using the same ballot for everyone. Supporters may feel ignored when they have to wait for another vote.

Title: A First Installation
Description: An OSI in another city wants to install Courtyard Vote today. Your installation guide is still unfinished. What will you do first?
First option tooltip: You get your first installation outside the pilots. The team loses time for launch work.
Second option tooltip: A tested guide makes future installs easier. This association may pick another tool while it waits.

Title: A Disputed Count
Description: The losing side says the vote was rigged. They want a recount they can trust. How will you answer them?
First option tooltip: Residents can check the count themselves. Anonymising the full log takes staff time.
Second option tooltip: An outside auditor can verify the tally. The review costs 200 and takes weeks.
